official.deadline_note: Direct-to-SSHRC deadline for the October 2026 competition is October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern), because the standard October 17 agency deadline falls on a weekend in 2026. Applications routed through a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota must meet that institution's internal deadline, which SSHRC warns is often significantly earlier than the agency deadline; scholarship liaison officers can forward institutional applications to SSHRC until 8:00 p.m. eastern on December 7.
official.application_cycle: October 2026 competition, Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS)
official.status_note: SSHRC lists the October 2026 competition as open, with a direct-to-agency deadline of October 19, 2026 (8:00 p.m. eastern) and an institutional route; applicants are notified of results by April 30.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published pages state only value and duration ($40,000 per year for 3 years); no tuition coverage is published for the core award.
benefits: Indigenous Scholars Supplement valued at $5,000 for one year for eligible Indigenous CGRS D award holders applying through NSERC or SSHRC
Each agency holds up to 10 additional awards reserved for Black student researchers who self-identify and consent

Affiliated supplements and joint initiatives, including the Aileen D. Ross Fellowship ($10,000), the Queen's Fellowship ($10,000), DND MINDS Doctoral Awards ($40,000 per year, up to 36 months), Sport Participation Research Initiative supplements and Mitacs training access
Available start dates are the first of May, September or January, and awards may be held part time on agency approval
eligibility: Completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study in the program for which funding is requested by December 31 of the calendar year of application

Enrolled in, or applying to, a predominantly research-oriented doctoral program leading to a thesis, dissertation, scholarly publication, performance, recital and/or exhibit merit-reviewed by a panel of experts at the institution

Apply through a Canadian institution with a doctoral award quota for the chosen agency, or directly to CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC, depending on registration status during the calendar year of application; applications submitted through the incorrect channel will be rejected
Apply to only one CRTAS program (CGRS M, CGRS D or CPRA) per academic year, and a maximum of three times to the CGRS D program
Must not already have received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC, including a Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship
International applicants must be registered in their doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline; up to 15% of awards are available to international applicants
requirements: Complete and verify the online Canada Graduate Research Scholarship-Doctoral application form and the SSHRC web-based CV (every page must be saved and verified; unverified sections block submission)
Two referees must each complete a one-page Letter of Appraisal form online before the deadline; the application cannot be verified or submitted until both are complete
Submit through the correct channel for the applicant's registration status, using SSHRC's online system before 8:00 p.m. eastern on October 19 for direct applications
Attach all required PDFs meeting the published page-length, margin, font and file-size specifications (500 Kb maximum per file)
documents: Online application form and SSHRC web CV
Research proposal, maximum two pages (PDF, unprotected, 500 Kb maximum, 12 pt Times New Roman, 3/4 inch margins)
Bibliography and citations, maximum five pages
Research contributions, relevant experience and activities, maximum two pages
Up-to-date official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate studies (registrar-issued, fall session of the year of application or after the last completed term)
Two Letters of Appraisal, one page each, completed by referees online
Allowable inclusions (special circumstances) and official registrar letter confirming part-time study or leave of absence, if applicable, maximum one page each
One-page justification for each supplement or joint initiative selected, if applicable
selection_criteria: Research potential (50%): quality of the research proposal, feasibility and soundness of methodology, significance and expected contributions, quality of contributions, critical judgment, ethical conduct, originality and initiative, communication ability

Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia (50%): relevant training, scholarships and distinctions, academic record and transcripts, and professional, academic and extracurricular activities and collaborations
Applications are evaluated by agency-specific merit review committees; institutional applications undergo an institutional review before being forwarded within the institution's quota
coverage: Published value and duration: $40,000 per year for 3 years (36 months), paid as a stipend to the award holder

Awards held at eligible Canadian institutions are paid by the institution on its own payment schedule, with no portion withheld without the award holder's consent except for tax purposes; awards held outside Canada are paid directly by the agency in twice-yearly instalments
Associated supplements and joint initiatives are offered separately and are not part of the core award
application_method: Determine the correct channel from registration status during the calendar year of application and whether the institution holds a doctoral award quota for the chosen agency
Register and log in to SSHRC's online system, complete the application form and SSHRC web CV, verifying each page
Invite two referees, who complete their Letter of Appraisal forms online before the deadline

Upload the research proposal, bibliography, contributions, transcripts and any justification attachments, then submit before 8:00 p.m. eastern on October 19, 2026 (direct route) or by the institution's internal deadline
official.application_route: Select CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC by research subject matter, then apply through a Canadian institution holding a doctoral award quota (by that institution's earlier internal deadline) or directly to the agency by 8:00 p.m. eastern on October 19, 2026.
official.study_mode: Full-time doctoral study (award holders may request to hold the award part time, subject to individual agency approval)
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons may apply through their institution or directly; international applicants must be registered in a doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. Up to 15% of awards are available to international applicants, who must be registered in their doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline; only Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons may hold the award at a degree-granting institution outside Canada.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must choose the one federal granting agency (CIHR, NSERC or SSHRC) that best matches their research subject matter, and may apply to only one CRTAS program per academic year; SSHRC covers social sciences and humanities subject matter.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of maximum two pages written in clear, plain language for a multidisciplinary committee, plus a bibliography and citations attachment of maximum five pages; the program of study must be predominantly research-oriented and lead to a merit-reviewed thesis, dissertation, scholarly publication, performance, recital and/or exhibit.
official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship-Doctoral program recognizes and supports the next generation of outstanding innovators, knowledge workers, creative thinkers and researchers; by providing support for a high-quality research training experience to awardees, the program strives to foster impacts within and beyond the research environment.
official.program_type: Federal doctoral research training scholarship in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite (harmonized CGRS-D, jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC)
official.english_requirement: No English or French test score is published. The application may be submitted in either of Canada's official languages, English or French, and supporting documents written in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a certified English or French translation.

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage: the official pages publish only value, duration and payment mechanics, with no statement of what the stipend covers
travel_coverage: no travel allowance is published for the core award (research travel supplements exist only as separate associated opportunities)
institutional deadlines: each Canadian institution sets its own, so no central figure is published
verification.notes: Value ($40,000 per year for 3 years) and the October 19, 2026 direct deadline were verified on SSHRC's CGRS-D page and the shared tri-agency competition details page; channel rules, document specifications, language rules, selection criteria and supplement values were verified on SSHRC's October 2026 applicant instructions, and payment/instalment rules on the tri-agency research training award holder's guide.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipend-only doctoral award: $40,000 a year for up to three years, paid through your institution and taxable, with no tuition remission attached. The application is merit-reviewed 50% on research potential and 50% on experience, so the two-page proposal written for non-specialists carries as much weight as your publication record. Your submission channel is determined by where you were registered during the 2026 calendar year, and applying through the wrong channel gets the file rejected without review.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral students in the social sciences and humanities early in their degree (36 months of study or fewer by December 31, 2026) with a feasible, well-scoped research proposal.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your registration status for the whole of calendar year 2026 and whether your institution holds a doctoral award quota for SSHRC; this alone decides whether you apply internally or directly to SSHRC by October 19
Ask your faculty of graduate studies for its internal deadline now; SSHRC warns institutional deadlines are often significantly earlier than the agency's
Line up two referees weeks in advance and warn them to check spam filters for the system-generated Letter of Appraisal invitation, since you cannot submit until both forms are verified
Draft the proposal in plain language for a multidisciplinary committee: specific research questions, sound methodology, significance and feasibility inside two pages
Compress every PDF under 500 Kb, use 12 pt Times New Roman with 3/4 inch margins, and open each uploaded file to confirm it is not corrupted
If you studied part-time or interrupted your degree, request the registrar's letter confirming registration-status dates now; no months are deducted without it
common_rejection_risks: Submitting through the wrong channel: registration status during the calendar year, not where you plan to hold the award, decides institution-versus-direct, and misfiled applications are deemed ineligible
Exceeding 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study by December 31, 2026, including months counted from a joint program's master's portion
Referee Letters of Appraisal arriving late, which blocks verification and submission of the whole application
Applying to more than one CRTAS program in the same academic year, in which case only the first eligible application is retained
PDF attachments breaching page-length, margin, font or 500 Kb limits, which renders the application ineligible on formatting alone
Submitting to the wrong agency, or to SSHRC for subject matter NSERC or CIHR should review
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, ancillary fees and living costs beyond the $40,000 annual stipend must be funded from other sources: the published core award carries no tuition waiver, no research allowance and no travel supplement, and no tax is withheld at source, so awardees must set aside funds for their tax bill.
document_audit: Transcripts must be registrar-issued and dated in the fall of the application year (or after your last completed term); an institution without transcripts must supply a sealed or dean-signed letter covering program, registration status, start date and degree sought
Non-English or French transcripts, and titles of publications in other languages, need certified translations
Research proposal is capped at two pages and the bibliography at five; the contributions and experience statement shares a single two-page allowance, so select only what advances your case
Part-time study or approved leave needs a one-page registrar letter combined with the transcript PDF, or every month counts as full-time
alerts: The 2026 direct deadline moved from October 17 to October 19 (8:00 p.m. eastern) because October 17 falls on a weekend; institutional applicants should note the separate December 7 forwarding deadline
SSHRC's acknowledgement email arrives four to six weeks after the deadline, and you can download your completed application for only 30 days after the deadline
Late applications are never accepted and no content can be changed after submission, only personal contact details by email
You may apply to this program a maximum of three times, and any prior tri-agency doctoral scholarship (including Vanier) makes you ineligible
The award can only start on May 1, September 1 or January 1 and cannot precede your program start date; holding it part time or deferring it requires agency approval
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete and verify the SSHRC online form and web CV, have both referees submit their appraisals, upload all PDFs, then submit electronically before the deadline; institutions review their applicants first and forward only quota-limited nominations.

official.deadline_note: SGS publishes no single deadline: the student deadline and application dates are set by each graduate unit (see the SGS student-deadlines list), the graduate unit must forward all OGS nominations to SGS by the Graduate Unit Deadline set in the SGS Memo, and results are announced in mid-July.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 award year (cycle currently advertised by SGS, with a live student information session on November 12, 2026)
official.status_note: SGS presents the OGS competition as running for the 2027-2028 award year: applicants must be registered or intend to register full-time in 2027-2028, graduate units set their own student deadlines, and results are released in mid-July.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The published value is $5,000 per session. Payments are issued through ACORN in equal instalments at the start of each academic session; January and May instalments are posted to the student's fees account and applied automatically to tuition and outstanding charges with any remainder refunded, while September instalments are released in full unless there are arrears.
benefits: $5,000 per session, giving $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three consecutive sessions
Jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, with the awarding graduate unit contributing one-third of the total award cost

Automatic consideration for the SGS Inclusive Excellence Graduate Scholarship competition for graduate students who are Black and/or Indigenous to Canada and identify as such on the OGS application, where Ontario Graduate Scholarships are valued at up to $15,000 per year and other SGS awards at $10,000 per year, with approximately 25 awards made annually
Applicants may consent to have their OGS application used for other U of T graduate award competitions, including QEII-GSST
eligibility: Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the graduate unit's student deadline, OR an international student at U of T on a temporary resident visa (study permit) whose valid permit is effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline

Registered, or intending to register, full-time in an eligible program in 2027-2028, defined as a full-time program of two or three terms leading to a graduate degree (full-time means at least 60% of a full course load, or 40% for students with a permanent disability)

At least A- (or equivalent) in each of the last two completed years of study (full-time equivalent), or an overall A- average on all graduate courses completed if two or more years of graduate study are complete
Have not exceeded the lifetime maximum of six years of government-funded support, or the maximum OGS/QEII support for the current level of study (two years at master's, four at doctoral)
In good standing with the Ontario Student Assistance Program; those with an OSAP restriction must clear it within 30 days of notification to accept and hold the award
requirements: Submit an OGS application to the proposed graduate unit using the SGS centralized online OGS application, meeting that unit's internal submission deadline
All application components must be completed online; the application can only be submitted once both Academic Assessments are complete
Provide two academic references who submit their Academic Assessment online; each referee has 60 days from the email request before the link expires
documents: OGS application form (submitted to the proposed graduate unit)

Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions scanned into a single PDF, including U of T transcripts; unofficial, student-issued or web transcripts are permitted, with one copy of the grading legend per transcript and no encrypted or digitally signed files
Previous awards, publications, conference presentations and research experience
Plan of study, maximum one page, plus a maximum one page for bibliography and citations
Two academic references submitted online as Academic Assessments
Certified English translation for transcripts written in a language other than English or French
selection_criteria: Relevant experience and achievements obtained within and beyond academia, weighted up to 40% (transcripts, academic accomplishments, prior awards, publications and presentations, research and creative productivity, training and work experience, extracurricular and community activity)
Plan of Study, weighted up to 30% (motivation, creativity, communication, feasibility, merit and significance, and synergy with the program of study)
Academic Assessment Reports, weighted up to 30% (15% for each letter) covering ability to complete the project on time, critical thinking, judgment, originality, autonomy and communication
Mandatory requirements: a plan of study and two academic assessments
coverage: Value of $5,000 per session, so $10,000 for two consecutive sessions or $15,000 for three consecutive sessions

Payments are administered by SGS and issued to students through ACORN in equal instalments at the start of each academic session; January and May instalments are applied first to tuition and outstanding charges with the remainder refunded, and September instalments are released in full unless the holder has arrears
Each scholarship is tenable for one year, that is two consecutive or three academic sessions, with each session four months in duration; the value and duration are detailed in the award offer letter
application_method: Log in to the SGS OGS application system (UTORid for current and previous U of T students, JOINid or a social login for admissions applicants) using an up-to-date browser, preferably in incognito mode

Create the Ontario Graduate Scholarship form, entering the faculty, graduate unit, program, level and year of study for the 2027-2028 academic year, and select the expected award start session (usually September)
Upload all transcripts as a single PDF, plus the research contributions PDF (maximum two pages) and the plan of study PDF (one page plus one page of references)
Enter the two referees to trigger online Academic Assessment requests, with a requested completion date well ahead of the graduate unit deadline
Submit to the proposed graduate unit by that unit's internal deadline; create a separate application for each graduate unit applied to
official.application_route: Complete the SGS centralized online OGS application and submit it to the proposed graduate unit (one application per unit) by that unit's student deadline.
official.study_mode: Full-time (at least 60% of a full course load, or 40% for students with a permanent disability)
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) by the graduate unit's student deadline; international students studying or planning to study at U of T on a temporary resident visa (student study permit) are eligible for a set number of OGS awards, with a valid permit effective as of the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only for a set number of awards. International applicants must hold an approved, valid study permit by the graduate unit's OGS international application deadline; a permit still pending approval at that date makes the applicant ineligible for the year's competition.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction: the program covers all disciplines of academic study at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario, and each graduate unit determines whether its programs are eligible for its OGS competition.
official.research_requirement: A plan of study of maximum one page (plus one page of references and citations) describing the proposed research project or plan of studies; thesis-stream applicants outline background, objectives, methodology, significance and expected contribution, while non-thesis applicants describe their course and research plan and rationale.
official.duration: One year: two consecutive or three academic sessions (each session is four months)
official.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines of academic study since 1975; at the University of Toronto the scholarship program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University, with the Province allocating to each university the number of awards it may offer annually.
official.program_type: Provincial merit scholarship (Government-Funded Award; Admission, In-Course, Master's and Doctoral categories at U of T)
official.english_requirement: No English test score is published. Transcripts written in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by a certified English translation, and titles and journal names of publications in other languages must be translated.

not_confirmed: central deadline: SGS publishes none; student deadlines are set individually by each graduate unit and the forwarding deadline sits in an internal SGS Memo
living_cost_coverage and travel_coverage: the published pages give value, duration, instalment mechanics and repayment rules only, with no statement that the award covers living or travel costs
specific graduate unit deadlines: the SGS student-deadlines list is a separate published spreadsheet and is not reproduced on the award page
verification.notes: Value ($5,000 per session, $10,000 for two sessions, $15,000 for three), duration, eligibility, selection criteria, required components, payment schedule and Inclusive Excellence consideration were verified on the SGS Ontario Graduate Scholarship page; transcript rules, login options, referee mechanics and plan-of-study limits were verified on the SGS OGS Application Instructions page.

applicant_utility.summary: The OGS is a modest but renewable-feeling merit award of $5,000 per academic session, worth $10,000 to $15,000 if you hold it across two or three sessions, and it is decided at the department level before anything reaches the province. Everything hinges on your graduate unit: it sets the deadline, decides whether your program is even eligible, adjudicates domestic applications, and nominates only a limited number of international files to SGS. Because the award cannot be held alongside SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR, Vanier or QEII-GSST money, treat it as a complement to a bigger doctoral fellowship rather than a substitute for one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving students (A- or better in recent years) entering or continuing a U of T master's or doctoral program whose department runs an OGS competition, including international students who already hold a valid study permit.
application_readiness_checklist: Find your unit's student deadline on the SGS student-deadlines list before doing anything else, then work backwards two weeks for referee letters

Create a separate OGS application for every graduate unit you are applying to; the award is not transferable between units or universities, and referees must complete a separate Academic Assessment for each
Send referee requests early and give a requested completion date ahead of your unit deadline, since the assessment link expires 60 days after it is sent and you cannot submit until both are complete

Assemble one unencrypted PDF of every post-secondary transcript, including U of T records, with a single grading legend per institution and certified translations for any non-English or French transcript
Write the plan of study to exactly one page plus one page of references, tailored to what the reviewing department looks for
International applicants: confirm the study permit approval date on record, not just the application date, against the unit's international deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the graduate unit's internal deadline; there is no central deadline to appeal to and late files are not carried forward
Assuming an OGS offer from one department or university travels with you; awards are not transferable, so each application must be made separately
Study permit not yet approved by the unit's international deadline, which makes the whole year's competition out of reach
An OSAP restriction, Canada Student Loan default or overpayment; restrictions must be cleared within 30 days of notification or the award is lost
Falling short of the A- minimum without documenting special circumstances for a unit-level exception
Dropping to part-time, withdrawing or finishing degree requirements early, which triggers repayment of the instalment for the incomplete session
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and living costs: at $5,000 per session the award does not approach U of T graduate tuition plus Toronto living costs, so it must be combined with a departmental funding package, a tri-agency or Vanier award, or personal funds. January and May instalments are also applied to outstanding fees first, so treat them as a partial fee offset rather than cash in hand.
document_audit: Transcripts must be one PDF containing every institution, including U of T, and must show the grading legend once per transcript; encrypted, digitally signed or corrupt PDFs cannot be viewed by your unit and may render the file ineligible
Transfer or exchange credit without grades requires the original transcript from the other institution in the package
The research contributions upload and the plan of study each have their own page limits and 500 Kb file caps; overflowing either is a silent formatting failure
Publications in languages other than English or French need translated titles and journal names so reviewers can weigh them
alerts: Applications are adjudicated by the department first and only forwarded to a centralized provincial competition, so department-level odds vary far more than the headline provincial numbers suggest
Results arrive in mid-July, after most admission offers, and Inclusive Excellence consideration runs to July 31; do not assume a rejection before then

You cannot hold an OGS in the same session or award year as SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR, Vanier or QEII-GSST funding, including awards continuing from a previous year, and all such years count against the lifetime six-year maximum
Applicants with OSAP restrictions may apply but must clear the restriction within 30 days of notification to accept the award
Award holders typically holding full-time paid employment are ineligible, and accepting research assistantships or part-time teaching is allowed only where unit policy permits
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Log in to the SGS OGS system, submit the completed application and both referee assessments to the proposed graduate unit by its internal deadline; the unit adjudicates, then forwards its limited nominations to SGS for the centralized competition, with results in mid-July.
